h1: Kessiri Hotel Sisaket — an affordable 3-star city hotel with free parking and easy access in central Sisaket
intro: If you're road-tripping through lower Isan and want a budget-friendly place in central Sisaket with parking and easy access, the name Kessiri Hotel comes up often in local reviews · It's a 3-star hotel on Khu Khan Road in the Mueang Tai subdistrict, in the Huai Nam Kham area · What guests mention most is that it sits right on a main road into town, has plenty of free parking and an on-site restaurant and cafe, and is only about 1 km from the Sisaket Aquarium · 50 rooms with air conditioning, refrigerator, water heater and free Wi-Fi, from approx. ฿500/night · Real guest reviews say it's clean and good value, though the rooms are fairly compact.

body.html: Kessiri Hotel is a 3-star, 50-room hotel in central Sisaket, on Khu Khan Road in the Mueang Tai subdistrict, in the Huai Nam Kham area · Its main draw is its location right on a main road into town and its generous free parking, which makes it a popular choice for drivers touring lower Isan and travellers stopping for a single night en route · It isn't a luxury hotel, but it's a practical, clean and affordable place to stay.

Rooms come as Deluxe with either a king bed or twin beds · Each has air conditioning, a refrigerator, a water heater, a TV and blackout curtains that help you sleep even in the daytime · What guests praise most often is that the rooms are clean, well-equipped and the staff are friendly · Free Wi-Fi in every room · Worth knowing from reviews: the rooms are fairly compact compared with newer hotels in town, and some guests find the beds a touch soft — a matter of personal taste.
"Budget-friendly, clean rooms, lots of parking, right on a main road so it's easy to get in and out, with cafes and restaurants nearby and polite, friendly staff — great for drivers stopping over."

Location is another reason guests pick it · In the Huai Nam Kham area, it's only about 1 km from the Sisaket Aquarium and roughly 1.8 km from Wat Phra That Rueang Rong · The hotel is surrounded by restaurants, coffee shops and convenience stores, so finding food is easy · On site there's a restaurant and cafe, luggage storage, laundry and a taxi-booking service — handy for anyone who doesn't want to head out again after a long day of driving.

Honestly, from real reviews: Kessiri has been open a long time and parts of it are showing their age · Some older reviews mention rooms that feel dated, a musty smell in a few rooms, and inconsistent hot water or air conditioning, while many more recent reviews say it has been refreshed and is cleaner · Room consistency is something to allow for — ask to see the room at check-in if you can · Also note that there's no breakfast service and no swimming pool; if you need either, look elsewhere.

In short, if you want a place in central Sisaket in the few-hundred-baht range, with free parking and easy access, and you're not fussy about compact or slightly dated rooms, Kessiri Hotel is a sensible stopover · A score of around 7.7 from 127 reviews captures it well: good value, good location, easy parking — just don't expect luxury or large rooms · It suits visitors heading to the aquarium, people in town on business, or anyone breaking up a lower-Isan road trip.

A tip from following the reviews here: if you're booking several rooms or travelling as a group, call the hotel directly about room condition and ask for a refurbished room, since room quality varies · And because there's no breakfast on site, head out to one of the morning eateries or coffee shops along Khu Khan Road and the Huai Nam Kham area for a proper Sisaket-style breakfast — better value and tastier too.

honestSummary: Kessiri Hotel is a solid choice for anyone who wants an affordable place in central Sisaket with free parking, easy access and an on-site restaurant — clean, good value and close to the aquarium · But you have to accept the compact rooms, an ageing building, and no breakfast or pool; it suits a stopover more than being the destination of your trip.
honestChecks: If you expect large, newly furnished rooms — rooms here are fairly compact and some are showing their age → ask for a refurbished room when booking, or look at newer boutiques in town if your budget allows.
If you want breakfast or a pool — there's neither here → there are morning eateries and cafes nearby to walk to, so allow time to head out.
If you're driving yourself or stopping over on a lower-Isan road trip — the free parking and main-road location make it very convenient → this is the main reason guests pick Kessiri.

faqTitle: Frequently Asked Questions — Kessiri Hotel Sisaket

faq.q: Where is Kessiri Hotel in Sisaket, and what's nearby?
faq.a: Kessiri Hotel is at 1102-05 Khu Khan Road, Mueang Tai subdistrict, in the Huai Nam Kham area of central Sisaket · It's about 1 km from the Sisaket Aquarium and roughly 1.8 km from Wat Phra That Rueang Rong · Sisaket Train Station and the railway market are about a 5-minute drive away · It sits on a main road into town, with restaurants and convenience stores around it.

faq.q: How much does Kessiri Hotel cost, and what rooms are available?
faq.a: Rates start at approx. ฿500/night for a Deluxe room with a king bed · Deluxe twin rooms and refurbished rooms run around ฿540–฿650, with family/multi-guest rooms higher · Prices vary by date and room type, so compare Agoda, Booking and Trip.com before booking.

faq.q: Does Kessiri Hotel have parking and a restaurant?
faq.a: Yes to both · The hotel has plenty of free parking and an on-site restaurant and cafe · It's on Khu Khan Road, a main road into town, so it's easy to get in and out — ideal for drivers or a stopover on a lower-Isan road trip · However, there's no breakfast service and no swimming pool.

faq.q: Who is Kessiri Hotel best for?
faq.a: It's best for travellers who want an affordable, few-hundred-baht place in central Sisaket with free parking for a one-night stopover · It suits drivers, aquarium visitors, or people in town on business · It's less suited to anyone wanting large rooms, a newer hotel, breakfast or a pool.

faq.q: Are the rooms at Kessiri Hotel clean, and what should I know?
faq.a: Most recent reviews say the rooms are clean, well-equipped and the staff are friendly · Worth knowing: the building has been open a long time and some rooms are showing their age, so room quality is inconsistent · Ask for a refurbished room when booking and check the room at check-in if you can.

faq.q: Is parking convenient at Kessiri Hotel if I'm driving?
faq.a: Very · The hotel is on Khu Khan Road, a main road into town, with plenty of free parking and easy access · This is the main reason road-trippers through lower Isan choose Kessiri as their Sisaket stopover.
